newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Bids flat to lower, sales slow.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Bids flat to lower, sales slow.

text.p: Bids for hard red winter wheat were steady to lower on Friday and movement slowed amid calls for a lower KCBT opening, several High Plains grain dealers said.
"We had pretty good movement yesterday afternoon after the board closed up six," an Oklahoma dealer said. "We haven't seen much this morning but they're selling rallies pretty good around here."
Dealers noted the Wheat Quality Council annual spring wheat tour found spring and durum yield potential was lower than last year's tour estimate.

The tour pegged spring wheat yield potential at 31.3 bushels per acre, down from 36.4 bushels estimated on last year's tour. They estimated durum yield potential at 27.7 bushels per acre, against 29.7 last year.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: U=KCBT September. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
